# The radius of a BallVector of two limbs times a number of T

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `bv_scale_radius_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Numbers of `T` that bound expressions of $m, r_x, a$ from above:

$$r_z \ge \lvert a\rvert r_x + \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})} (1 + u) + \frac{\mathrm{tiny}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})}.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `bv_scale_2`, called by `x * a`, `a * x`, `x *= a`, `scale(x, a, z)` and `axpy` of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $m \ge 0$.
- $r_x \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r_z \ge \lvert a\rvert r_x + \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})} (1 + u) + \frac{\mathrm{tiny}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})}$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `bv_scale_radius_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/BvRadius.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/BvRadius.v), against `bv_scale_radius_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions bv_scale_radius_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition bv_scale_radius_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall m rx a : R,
  fmt emin prec m ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  0 <= m ->
  0 <= rx ->
  let rz := bv_scale_radius_2 emin prec tie_even m rx a in
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  ((((Rabs a) * rx) + (((m * (2 * u prec ^ 2)) / (1 - (2 * u prec ^ 2))) * (1 + u prec))) + ((1 * eta emin) / (1 - (2 * u prec ^ 2)))) <= rz.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `bv_scale_radius_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the radius lines of ball_scale_2 (Milestone 1, second radius design), at the largest magnitude of a center of the result (milestone2.md, BallVector). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/bv_scale_radius_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/bv_scale_radius_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The one radius of a BallVector with 2-limb centers times a number a of T (milestone2.md,
# "BallVector": bv_scale_radius_k): the radius lines of ball_scale_2, with m, the largest magnitude
# of the leading limb of a center of the result, in place of one entry's |cz0|. Every operation is a
# rounding of a nondecreasing function of m on nonnegative values, so with m the largest |cz0| the
# result is the largest of the radii that ball_scale_2 returns entry by entry. Its claim is what
# makes it a radius of every entry: by the bound of mul_2_1 relative to the result, an entry whose
# exact center is s = cx a and computed center cz has |cz - s| <= U |cz| + T <= U (1 + u) m + T, with
# U = unit/(1 - unit) and T = tiny/(1 - unit), and a member x a of the exact product is within
# |a| rx of s. The program gives a (an entry kernel): it is only multiplied, after its magnitude.

aa = abs(a)
p  = prod(aa, rx)
t  = fma(m, const up(unit(mul_2_1)/(1-unit(mul_2_1))*(1+u)), p)
rz = fma(t, const up((1+u)^3), const up((1+u)*((1+u)^2*eta+tiny(mul_2_1)/(1-unit(mul_2_1))+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))
```

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.
